transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-14 14:30 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Pike (Redwood, AE), Maya Chen (Redwood, SE), Sofia Ramirez (OrchidLane, Head of Security), Tom Becker (OrchidLane, Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (OrchidLane, CTO)

[00:00] Jordan Pike: Hey team, thanks for carving out time. uh quick intro — I'm Jordan from Redwood, today with Maya our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks. I'm Maya, I focus on private & dedicated deployments and KMS patterns.
[00:18] Sofia Ramirez: Hi. Sofia here. We run security for OrchidLane. We wanted to go through posture and make sure we won't run into surprises if we evaluate Redwood.
[00:25] Aisha Khan: Hi — Aisha, CTO. We're evaluating hosted first, but likely need options for dedicated or private depending on data residency and regs.
[00:32] Tom Becker: Tom — I'll be the hands-on infra person if we move forward.

[00:40] Jordan Pike: Great. Agenda — quick discovery on compliance and hosting constraints, talk through SSO/SAML and RBAC, KMS/encryption and BYOK options, audit logs and retention, and then next steps. Sound ok?
[00:50] Sofia Ramirez: Yup. We'll kick off with SOC2 and certifications.

[01:02] Maya Chen: To start — Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, our most recent report covers control categories around availability, confidentiality, and incident response. We also have ISO discussions but our formal ISO 27001 is in progress — ETA Q4.
[01:20] Sofia Ramirez: Can you share the SOC2 report and do you do a security questionnaire? We'll be running a vendor risk assessment with our GRC team.
[01:28] Jordan Pike: Absolutely — I'll share a redacted SOC2 and our security whitepaper after this call. We also have a vendor questionnaire template we can fill, and an NDA if needed for the full artefacts.

[01:45] Tom Becker: On hosting — OrchidLane handles credit card tokens and PII in certain features; for those flows we need either customer-managed keys or on-prem options. How do you handle KMS and BYOK?
[01:58] Maya Chen: Right. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS by default; we also support BYOK via customer KMS — we can integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and customers' HSM-backed keys via a bring-your-own-key flow. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can control the keys entirely — we can support HSM-backed KEKs.
[02:18] Sofia Ramirez: Do you have attestations for HSM usage and the process?
[02:22] Maya Chen: We have design docs and integration guides. The BYOK flow has an initial key import and periodic rotation steps; the key never leaves the customer's KMS. We'll share the terraform snippet and the sequence diagram.

[02:36] Aisha Khan: Important for us is separation of model weights vs customer data. Does Redwood persist raw customer payloads in logs or store them long-term?
[02:47] Jordan Pike: Good question. By default, Hosted retains logs for telemetry and helps debugging, but we have controls for log retention and redaction. For customers handling PII, we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can enforce no-persist policies and control KV cache eviction. We also support a redact-on-ingest pipeline for hosted with configurable rules.
[03:08] Tom Becker: For compliance we need an ability to pull audit logs into our SIEM and keep them for seven years for eDiscovery — is log export supported?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Yes — audit logs are exportable via S3 push or via our log connector to common SIEMs. Retention is configurable; we'll need to talk about storage costs for long-term retention, but technically supported.

[03:32] Sofia Ramirez: On identity — we run Okta, require SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups. RBAC must allow environment-level and route-level controls, ability to lock down model access by team.
[03:46] Maya Chen: We support SAML2 and SCIM. RBAC maps to roles you define; you can create granular roles for model access, per-route access, and token scoping. In Private deployments you get full LDAP/AD integration for fine-grained permissions.
[04:00] Jordan Pike: To add — we also offer session-level audit for token use and per-token cost attribution in the console. That helps link a request to a user and team for audits.

[04:12] Tom Becker: How are API keys rotated, and what's the rotation cadence? We prefer automated rotation enforced by a policy.
[04:18] Maya Chen: API keys can be set to expire. For Dedicated & Private we integrate with customer secret manager and support short-lived tokens via our OIDC path; automated rotation is possible via our management api, which the terraform module can hook into.

[04:33] Sofia Ramirez: Encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for backend connections and VPC peering? We need strong network controls.
[04:41] Maya Chen: We use TLS 1.2+ for all external traffic; mTLS is available for Dedicated peerings and Private. VPC peering and private endpoints are supported for Dedicated and VPC-hosted Private installs.

[04:55] Aisha Khan: Adversarial question — what's your incident response posture if there's a suspected exfiltration?
[05:00] Jordan Pike: We have an IR plan: package includes contact channels, runbooks, and an escalation matrix. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide extended logging and forensic export on request. Incident SLAs differ by contract; we can bake additional obligations into an enterprise SLA.

[05:20] Tom Becker: From a runtime perspective, if we need to run inference on sensitive PII data, what are the operational differences between Hosted and Dedicated? Latency and cost aside, what's the security delta?
[05:31] Maya Chen: Security-wise: Hosted with BYOK + strict retention and redaction can be compliant for some customers, but Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, network isolation, and full control over keys and logs. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the maximal control if you need air-gap or regulatory isolation. The tradeoffs are management and cost.

[05:52] Sofia Ramirez: Are there known limitations re: model source code or weights residency? We need to know where model weights live for IP concerns.
[06:00] Maya Chen: Model weights for our curated open models are stored in encrypted object stores that we manage; for Dedicated you can choose to host weights in your environment, or we can use compressed quantized variants. We can provide a model residency matrix in the doc pack.

[06:18] Jordan Pike: Also, if you plan to vet our platform with a pen test, we welcome it — we have a standard process and a pre-approved scope.

[06:26] Sofia Ramirez: We'll likely request a limited pen test and a security questionnaire response. Also need clarity on data deletion workflow — if a user requests erasure, how do you propagate that to caches and logs?
[06:38] Maya Chen: We support an erase API that triggers KV cache purge, and we maintain deletion logs. On Hosted we have a background job to scrub telemetry; for Dedicated/Private you can enforce immediate eviction. We will document the deletion guarantees (time-to-delete targets) in the follow-up packet.

[06:56] Tom Becker: One practical item — network egress. We have strict outbound rules and need to know which IP ranges Redwood uses so we can update firewall rules.
[07:04] Jordan Pike: We'll include the IP ranges and region mapping in the security packet. For Dedicated we can provide turnkey private endpoints with static IPs.

[07:14] Aisha Khan: Curious about compliance for EU data residency — if data is from our EU customers, can we keep it in eu-west-1 and ensure no cross-border replication?
[07:22] Maya Chen: Yes, we have region pinning for Hosted but with caveats; Dedicated or Private gives stronger guarantees — no background cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled. We'll provide the region residency guarantees in writing.

[07:32] Jordan Pike: To wrap up, sounds like next steps: Jordan sends SOC2 and whitepaper, Maya shares KMS + terraform snippets, and we schedule a technical deep-dive with Tom and Aisha. Sofia will share the data classification spreadsheet. Any other asks?
[07:46] Sofia Ramirez: Could you also include a sample SLA and forensic export process?
[07:50] Jordan Pike: Will do.
[07:52] Aisha Khan: And a rough cost delta for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a 100 qps inference baseline would be useful before the deep-dive.
[07:59] Jordan Pike: We'll include a ballpark and a worksheet.

[08:06] Jordan Pike: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet by Monday.
[08:10] Sofia Ramirez: Thanks.
[08:12] Tom Becker: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes and transcription imperfections: occasional mis-heard product names ("Red wood" / "Redhood") and "K-V cache" variations in transcript; some timestamps approximate.

References mentioned: SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001 (in progress), KMS BYOK flow, terraform snippet, log export S3, SIEM connectors, redaction pipeline, erase API, model residency matrix, IP ranges, sample SLA, pen test process.

End of transcript.
